captured_from: A PostToolUse payload for a tool call made INSIDE a subagent, emitted by Claude Code 2.1.288 under `claude -p --model sonnet` in a scratch project (d:\pantesting\ctxmon-probe) whose only hook dumped its stdin; PAN was not installed there. The prompt ran one Bash call in the main thread and started one general-purpose subagent that ran one Bash call. The key set and nesting are copied from the subagent call's payload: `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `scratchpad_dir`, `prompt_id`, `permission_mode`, `agent_id`, `agent_type`, `hook_event_name`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_response`, `tool_use_id`, `duration_ms`. Values are neutral synthetic; the tool input and output are the probe's own marker command.

placeholders.{{SESSION_ID}}: the host session id; the same for the main thread and its subagents
placeholders.{{TRANSCRIPT_PATH}}: the MAIN session transcript — the host sends the main file even for a subagent's call
placeholders.{{AGENT_ID}}: the subagent's id; its own transcript is <dir of TRANSCRIPT_PATH>/<SESSION_ID>/subagents/agent-<AGENT_ID>.jsonl

notes: Two facts this payload carries for hooks/pan-context-monitor.js. (1) A subagent's call is marked by `agent_id` and `agent_type`; the main-thread call's payload in the same capture had neither. (2) `transcript_path` still names the main session's file and no `agent_transcript_path` is sent, so a hook that measures the subagent's context must derive the subagent's own file. The payload also carried `effort` as an object whose values were not recorded; it is omitted rather than invented, and no PAN hook reads it.
